# Introduction

## Business context

I am an entry-level analyst at an investment firm that finances **sustainable infrastructure** and applies **responsible-investment** principles. My line manager asked for four pieces of work:

1. Most common climate hazards affecting communities globally
2. Number of planned projects and total funding sought, by region
3. Ranked list of collaboration / investment opportunities
4. Best model to predict environmental controversy involvement, with evaluation

**How I will work.** For every step I first explain *why* I am doing it and *how*, then run the R code, then *interpret* the result. All data preparation is done in R (nothing is edited in Excel), and I never type in data values by hand; every number comes from the two CSV files.

## Load packages

```{r packages}
# Install and load packages

if(!require("pacman"))install.packages("pacman")

pacman::p_load(readr, dplyr, tidyr, stringr, lubridate, purrr, ggplot2, gridExtra, GGally, corrplot)
pacman::p_load(tidytext, textstem, wordcloud, textdata, topicmodels)
pacman::p_load(DescTools, skimr, finalfit, rstatix, huxtable, jtools)
pacman::p_load(knitr, easystats, gtsummary, gt, scales)
pacman::p_load(SnowballC, textstem)
pacman::p_load(caret, tibble)
```

# Data Import and Initial Inspection

## Import the dataset

```{r read-data}
projects_raw <- read_csv("env_projects.csv")
firms_raw <- read_csv("env_controversy.csv")
```

## Understanding Data

```{r initial-inspection}
dim(projects_raw)
dim(firms_raw)

str(projects_raw)
str(firms_raw)

glimpse(projects_raw)
glimpse(firms_raw)

head(projects_raw, 10)
head(firms_raw, 10)
```

**Interpretation.** `env_projects.csv` has `r nrow(projects_raw)` rows (one row = one planned project) and `r ncol(projects_raw)` columns; `env_controversy.csv` has `r nrow(firms_raw)` firms (one row per firm) and `r ncol(firms_raw)` columns.
